headline: EU leaders tell the Commission to find money for Ukraine in 2027
headline_short: EU seeks more money for Ukraine
deck: Ukraine puts next year's shortfall at 70 billion euros or more; Belgium still refuses to use frozen Russian assets.
standard: EU leaders asked the European Commission on Friday to propose how to close Ukraine's budget gap for 2027, said António Costa, president of the European Council, after the summit in Brussels. Ukraine puts its financial and military shortfall at 70 billion euros or more.
Last year 24 of the 27 EU countries, Denmark among them, agreed to borrow 90 billion euros for Ukraine for 2026 and 2027; the G7 and the IMF, which were to cover the rest, are slow to pay.
Mette Frederiksen, the prime minister, points to frozen Russian assets. Belgium, where most are held at Euroclear, a securities depository, refuses for fear of a Russian lawsuit.
short: EU leaders asked the European Commission on Friday to propose how to close Ukraine's budget gap for 2027, which Ukraine puts at 70 billion euros or more. Belgium still refuses to use frozen Russian assets.
